provenance.labelled_by: coding agent: painted-line trace (scripts/label_lane_rows.py) plus visual check of the drawn overlay
provenance.method: for each row, find the run of yellow paint on that scanline and follow it down the image; the trace is drawn back onto the photo and inspected before being accepted. The lane model is never loaded by the labeller.
provenance.why_left_only: On both images the ego lane's RIGHT paint leaves the frame before the bottom rows (highway_road: right edge exits at y~510; sir_image7: the white edge exits at y~520 and the right half carries a stock-photo watermark), so a right-boundary number would have to be invented. Only boundaries that are painted and inside the frame are labelled.
provenance.supersedes: labels/eval_labels.json -> lane_ego_boundaries. Those rows were read by eye and the right-boundary column was misread by 70-110 px (it followed the shoulder edge, not the paint). Any lane error computed against them before v1.4 is withdrawn; see EVALUATION.md 10.1.
provenance.coordinate_system: original image pixels (x, y), origin top-left; x is the centre of the painted stripe
provenance.limitations: 11 points on 2 photographs, one straight and one curving, no night, no rain, no construction zones. This measures boundary placement, not detection rate over a dataset.
